children: Airtel Money has announced to list 10% of its existing shares on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange (LSE). The International Finance Corporation (IFC) has agreed to purchase up to £67.2 million ($90 million) of shares at the final offer price under a cornerstone investment agreement.

The IPO comes against a backdrop of reports that Airtel Money has scaled back its fundraising ambitions. Bloomberg reported that the company is now seeking to raise at least $800 million, significantly below an earlier target of between $1.5billion and $2 billion, after investor feedback prompted a reduction in the valuation sought for the offering. The listing was also delayed earlier this year after parent company Airtel Africa pushed back plans for the flotation to the second half of 2026.

Citigroup Global Markets has been appointed sole sponsor, lead-left global coordinator and joint bookrunner, while Barclays, Bank of America Securities, Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan are acting as joint global coordinators and joint bookrunners. Additional bookrunners include Absa Bank, BNP Paribas, Emirates NBD Capital, First Abu Dhabi Bank, Jefferies and Standard Bank of South Africa, with BTIG serving as co-bookrunner.

The UAE remains central to Airtel Money’s pan-African operations and growth ambitions, with members of its senior leadership team and key functions based in the Emirates. Abu Dhabi-based Lunate holds an equity stake of approximately 2% in the business and the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) approximately 8%.

Airtel Africa, which currently owns 77.85% of Airtel Money, expects to remain a long-term strategic shareholder following the listing. In 2021, a group of investors including TPG, Mastercard, the Qatar Investment Authority and Chimetech Holding invested a combined $550 million in the fintech business.

Key figures include 53 million monthly active users, $213 billion in annual transaction value, $1.35 billion in revenue, $676 million in EBITDA, $373 million in net income and a $90 million cornerstone commitment from IFC.
The prospectus is slated for early October, with pricing anticipated later that month.
(Writing by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Dubai-based Airtel Money seeks London IPO, plans to float at least 10%
